transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
Tuesday is midterm election day
and it will determine the balance of power in Congress.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro says keep an eye on Alaska.
- Alaska is one of those places
that is looking really close right now.
Toss-up state, red state that Trump won,
but looks very, very close
and it counts votes very, very slowly.
It has rank choice voting.
They didn't decide their races
sometimes till three weeks later.
If we're stuck in a mess of three weeks
waiting to know control of the Senate,
there's gonna be a whole heck of a lot
of misinformation going on.
We know that President Trump's already laying the groundwork
to say that the election was rigged.
It's better to have decisive victories
one way or the other in this country
because close elections tend to now be contested.
- President Trump is traveling to Kansas and Iowa today
to lead in-person rallies.
After earlier deciding to do teler rallies instead.
The Gaza Ministry of Health reports
at least 143 Palestinians were killed
in Israeli attacks in Gaza last month.
NPR's Anis Baba reports from Gaza.
- A year after a ceasefire took effect,
Israeli airstrikes are killing Palestinians across Gaza.
Israel says it's targeting Hamas operatives.
On Sunday, five Palestinians were killed in southern Gaza
when an Israeli drone fired two missiles
at a group of Palestinian police officers.
According to Gaza's Ministry of Interior,
the officers were carrying out a raid
against a suspected drug dealer.
In a separate strike west of Gaza City,
three Palestinians were killed.
According to the Health Ministry,
a father and his four-year-old son were among those killed.
The boy's mother and sister were also critically injured.
Anis Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
- Investors will be gauging the strength
of both the job market and the tech sector this week.
NPR's Stephen Bissaha reports tech companies
are coming off of a steep sell-off.
- Apple will have its latest earnings call Monday.
It's a relatively smaller player in the AI space
compared to the other tech giants,
but investors will listen for what the company
has to say about supply issues.
The industry's AI build-out has driven up the price
of components like memory chips,
and that's led to Apple recently raising prices.
A disappointing earnings report from Chipmaker Intel
led to that company's stock dropping
more than 24% last week.
On Tuesday, we'll get new jobs data for September
from the labor department
into what's been a low-hire, low-fire market.
In August, both job openings and layoffs held steady.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
- The FBI says the billions of dollars stolen from Binance
in the biggest crypto heist in history
was orchestrated by North Korean hackers.
The bureau says this week's attack was tied
to malicious cyber activity
by an entity known as Trader Traitor.
The same entity was behind a $1.5 billion hack
against Bybit last year.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Golden State Valkyries
have won the WNBA Championship.
Ben Trefny reports from members stationed KALW
in San Francisco.
(crowd cheering)
- The Valk's defeated the Atlanta dream 68 to 63
in game seven of the finals.
The home crowd at the Chase Center in San Francisco
in a arena better known as Ballhala
was raucous throughout.
Golden State's top-ranked defense held the dream
and their star Angel Reese in check,
and they were driven by guard Gabby Williams,
who scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half,
the most by any WNBA player in a half
in postseason history.
This is just the Valkyries' second season,
and they became the fastest major
North American expansion team to win a title.
- For NPR News, I'm Ben Trefny in San Francisco.
- Legal challenges to President Trump's
proposed memorial arch continue to grow.
The District of Columbia and Virginia
have filed lawsuits in federal court yesterday,
even as the administration says construction
on the project could begin as early as next week.
There are now three lawsuits
calling for a halt to the project.
The arch would tower 250 feet
and would be located in the middle of a traffic circle
at the end of a bridge that spans the Potomac River.
That bridge connects Washington DC
with Arlington National Cemetery,
and is presently part of an unobstructed view
between the Lincoln Memorial and the cemetery.
Last night, President Trump said the arch
is very important militarily
for Washington DC and our country.
The original plans made no mention
of a military component to the arch.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
This message comes from BetterHelp,
an online therapy platform that gives you space
to talk about what's taking up too much of your brain.
BetterHelp is now in network
with more than 125 health plans.
Visit betterhelp.com/NPR.
Cost and coverage may vary.

topics.text: Midterm election day Tuesday; Alaska's slow, rank-choice count could delay Senate control
President Trump travels to Kansas and Iowa to hold in-person rallies
Gaza Health Ministry reports 143 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks last month
Israeli drone strike kills five Palestinian police officers in southern Gaza
Investors watch Apple earnings and September jobs data amid tech stock sell-off
FBI says North Korean hackers were behind the $1.5 billion Binance crypto heist
Golden State Valkyries win WNBA championship, defeating Atlanta Dream in game seven
District of Columbia and Virginia sue over Trump's 250-foot memorial arch project
